title: Grantham Institute Annual Lecture 2026 with Anne Hidalgo
desc:
Progress in the face of pushback

​Around the world, the leaders driving the most ambitious climate action are increasingly finding themselves at the centre of political polarisation, misinformation campaigns, and public backlash. Yet history shows that transformative change has rarely been achieved by following the path of least resistance. From redesigning cities and defending climate science to challenging vested interests, bold leadership often demands the willingness to go against the grain and withstand intense scrutiny.

title: Leadership in the Age of AI
desc:
The corporate world faces a growing engagement crisis. Around 80 percent of the global workforce is disengaged, depriving organisations of the passion, energy and commitment needed to unlock their full potential. Yet too many leaders remain focused on short-term results rather than building the soul of their organisation.

title: IDE Seminar Series – Dr Ben Singer
desc: Although many viruses can cause seasonally-recurring respiratory disease outbreaks with distinct epidemiological features, we lack full comparative understanding of the factors determining these features. Multiple dynamical regimes can permit endemic seasonal outbreaks of respiratory viruses, so characteristics such as transmission intensity, sensitivity to seasonal forcing, and the role of age and prior exposure in immunity can be challenging to resolve. We used time series data including the disruption to viral circulation during the COVID-19 pandemic to investigate transmission dynamics of 6 viruses, revealing differential buffering of virus re-emergence by population immunity persisting from prior endemic transmission. Calibrated models capture virus-specific re-emergence dynamics…

title: Dynamical Systems Seminar – George Stepaniants
desc:
Speaker : George Stepaniants

Title : Volterra Integral Equations and Memory Dependent Constitutive Laws

Abstract : We will discuss how Volterra integral equations arise naturally in partially observed dynamical systems with specific applications to multiscale materials. This will motivate the construction of surrogate machine learning operators for the time-dependent simulation of multiscale materials. Finally, we will explore new developments in the theory of Volterra integral equations and the insights they gives us into the nonlinear operators that these surrogates approximate.

title: Finance and Stochastics Seminar – Emilio Barucci
desc:
Speaker : Emilio Barucci

Title : Trading and optimal execution in futures and spot markets with cross impacts

Abstract : We study the inventory management of a trader operating in spot and futures markets when the futures basis vanishes at maturity and exhibits mean-reversion. The model distinguishes between the primary market, where new information is incorporated into prices, from the secondary market whose price contains a mean reverting basis component. We characterize the optimal trading strategy under both cash settlement and physical delivery. We show that access to the secondary market creates a statistical-arbitrage opportunity starting from zero initial wealth by allowing the trader to exploit the intertemporal mean reversion of the basis. title: Astrophysics Weekly Seminar: Prof. Ludovic van Waerbeke – Can dark energy emerge from the standard model of particle physics?
desc:
Title

Can dark energy emerge from the standard model of particle physics?

Abstract

The discovery of cosmic acceleration established dark energy as one of the central problems in cosmology. In the standard cosmological model, dark energy is described by a cosmological constant, yet its extremely small value remains difficult to reconcile with expectations from quantum field theory. Recent DESI results, combined with other cosmological probes, suggest that dark energy may evolve with cosmic time. In this talk, I will first review the observational evidence for dark energy, what current data tell us about its properties, and why evolving dark energy is theoretically challenging. I will then discuss the possibility that dark energy may not require a new particle or field, but could…

title: Nelder Fellow lecture series – Prof Ed Bueler (University of Alaska Fairbanks)
desc:
Prof Ed Bueler (University of Alaska Fairbanks) : New solver approaches for variational inequalities

Lectures will be held on Tuesdays: 20 Oct, 27 Oct, 3 Nov, 17 Nov, at 15:00.

Abstract: This four-lecture series introduces variational inequalities to a general applied mathematical audience, pursues their finite element solution, and applies them to a geophysical problem. Variational inequalities are partial differential equation weak forms, but subject to bounds on their solution(s). They reformulate how one might pose boundary conditions at a free location; where the conditions apply is now determined simultaneously along with the solution. title: SPC Seminar – Plasma – Farhat Beg (UCSD)
desc:
Speaker: Farhat Beg (UCSD)

Title: Proton Heating in Integrated Proton Fast Ignition Experiments

Abstract: Proton fast ignition (PFI) is an alternative inertial confinement fusion (ICF) concept that promises high gain suitable for inertial fusion energy applications. In this concept, a short-pulse, high-intensity laser is used to generate an energetic proton beam that efficiently couples’ energy into a pre-compressed fuel assembly. This enables ignition conditions to be reached with less stringent symmetry and driver energy requirements than in the conventional hot-spot approach.

We report on the first integrated PFI campaign at the Omega Laser Facility that included both the compression and ignition phases to measure the temperature increase in the compressed core due to proton…

title: Junior Analysis Seminar – Monica Tapia del Moral (Cambridge)
desc:

Abstract

The study of characteristic gluing was initiated by Aretakis, Czimek, and Rodnianski (2021), and has since proven to be an effective tool for constructing solutions to the Einstein equations. A remarkable example of this is the work of Kehle and Unger, who used it to construct solutions to the Einstein–Maxwell-charged scalar field system undergoing gravitational collapse to form an exactly extremal Reissner–Nordström black hole in finite time, disproving the so-called third law of black hole thermodynamics, and challenging the intuition that had prevailed for decades in much of the theoretical physics community.
